narrative.overview:
Night Operations Desk is a calm, high-readiness tactical workspace: deep petrol-blue surroundings, slate work surfaces, warm off-white type, and restrained semantic signals. It should feel like a shared guild station used during a live operation—not a game lobby, generic admin dashboard, or theatrical command center.

The interface is defense-first and decision-first. Enemy composition leads every matchup; fit, risk, validation, and turn order remain legible before expansion. Density is purposeful rather than cramped, monster artwork stays prominent as functional identification, and progressive disclosure keeps long-form playbook material available without slowing the first decision.

No gradients or neon effects belong in this world. Depth comes from tonal surface steps, thin borders, and controlled low-chroma shadows; color is reserved for operational meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Deep petrol environment with layered slate/petrol surfaces.
Copper actions and danger, aqua safe/counter signals, blue proven/fit signals, and amber caution.
Defense-led matchup hierarchy with decision signals visible while collapsed.
Compact operational density, warm text, and prominent monster portraits.
Quiet depth, restrained motion, and no gradients or neon.

rules.name: The Copper Means Act Rule
rules.body: Copper is reserved for action, enemy danger, destructive intent, and focus; never use it as ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Cool Signals Rule
rules.body: Aqua communicates safe counters, while blue communicates proven evidence or matchup fit; do not swap those meanings.

rules.name: The No Neon Rule
rules.body: Semantic colors stay desaturated and bounded by tonal surfaces or borders—never glow, bloom, or become fluorescent.

rules.name: The Two-Speed Type Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk names the mission; DM Sans carries the decision. Do not introduce a third display voice.

rules.name: The Labels Scan, Body Explains Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracking belongs to short operational labels only; never apply it to paragraphs, monster names, or user-entered content.

rules.name: The Defense Leads Rule
rules.body: Enemy composition appears before the proposed attack in reading order, visual emphasis, and mobile stacking.

rules.name: The Decision Before Documentation Rule
rules.body: Fit, risk, and turn order must be visible before builds, substitutions, evidence, or the full game plan.

rules.name: The Collapsed Utility Rule
rules.body: A closed strategy card must still answer whether the counter fits, how safe it is, what can fail, and what moves first.

rules.name: The Layer, Then Lift Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with surface tone and borders first; add shadow only when an element must detach from its current plane.

rules.name: The Quiet Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows remain dark, diffuse, and low-chroma. They never become a colored glow.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: Inner controls are always tighter than their container: controls at 8–10px sit inside cards at 14px and dialogs at 16px.

rules.name: The Shape Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Pills are reserved for compact status and filters; circles are reserved for identity or point status; dashed edges mean optional, wildcard, or empty.

rules.name: The One Signal per Meaning Rule
rules.body: Within a strategy record, copper means enemy/risk, aqua means counter/safe, blue means fit/proven, and amber means caution—never encode two different meanings with the same accent.

rules.name: The Portraits Are Data Rule
rules.body: Monster artwork is functional identification, not decoration; keep it visible, consistently sized, and element-bordered.

dos: Do lead every result with the enemy defense, then show the proposed attack and its decision signals.
Do use the real petrol surface ladder, thin slate borders, and quiet dark shadows to create depth.
Do reserve copper for action, defense danger, destructive intent, and focus.
Do keep safe/counter aqua, proven/fit blue, and caution amber semantically distinct.
Do keep minimum 44px touch targets, visible keyboard focus, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do preserve prominent monster artwork and elemental borders as identification aids.
donts: Don't use gradients, neon colors, colored glow, or pure-black gaming surfaces.
Don't hide fit, risk, validation, or turn order behind expansion.
Don't let long-form guidance outrank the collapsed decision layer.
Don't use copper as a decorative accent or apply semantic colors without a status meaning.
Don't turn every label into a pill; reserve pills for statuses and compact filters.
Don't add a third typeface or use uppercase tracked labels for prose.
